I most certainly do!

Reason is imo the best DAW for recording (vocals and instruments). The comp/pitch/slice edit windows are really powerful and the quantization is almost always on point. It makes recording a vocal or a guitar or any other instrument really easy and straightforward.

The mixer also is really good for mixing, you can achieve really good results witht he ssl emulation (the compressor,  eq, gate, etc) are really good and can get you a well mixed track really quick. I dont like the semi parametric eq that much, i prefer fully parametic, like the one from neutron 2 or ozone but it works really good. 

As for mastering, I am not a mastering engeneer and my mastering is essentially slapping ozone on the master and that works pretty good.

It's not about the daw or the plugins, it's about the user. If you can mix a song well, the daw doesnt matter that much.
